Welcome to Kingfisher School
Join Our School
What We Offer
Kingfisher School provides GCSE pathways in English, mathematics and Vocational Studies in addition to Functional Skills qualifications.
Kingfisher School provides a daily nutritious and delicious choice of meals, including breakfast, to support good dietary health for all learners.
Kingfisher School liaises with Local Authorities to support transport applications for our learners.
Kingfisher School supports learners holistically to develop the vital skills needed for lifelong success.
Learners at Kingfisher School participate in a broad range of vocational pathways and programmes to help them gain skills for life.
Weymouth Bay, the harbour and the Jurassic coast are less than 1 mile away and will provide excellent opportunities for educational trips and activities for learners.
Testimonials
I cannot express how grateful I am for this school. Every member of staff has been incredible: supportive, patient, and deeply understanding of the trauma she had faced. Through their care, communication, and consistent patience, she has not only settled but is truly excelling. The transformation has been remarkable—both at school and at home.
My child has been at Kingfisher for a year now, I cannot express how grateful I am for this school. The transformation has been remarkable—both at school and at home. She is now the happy, bright girl I fought so hard to protect, and I sincerely thank the Kingfisher team for helping her blossom.
My child started at Kingfisher School and came home after school for 2 weeks, he said I didn’t know schools like this existed. I feel like I walked through hell to get to heaven.
I don’t really know where to begin, but to say what a difference in Callum wanting to come to school because he feels so happy and comfortable in his new surroundings. I really wish there were more schools and staff like you all.
Kingfisher has afforded my child the chance to be seen, staff members endeavour to meet the needs of every child with inclusivity at the heart of everything they do!
Kingfisher is a fantastic school, accommodates every need of every learner. I for one can say moving my child here has benefited them in every way possible, helped them achieve their goals, makes friends and learn that school and learning can be fun.

About Kingfisher School
Our School
Kingfisher School is a Special Educational Needs school which is located in Weymouth. We support learners aged 9 years to 16 years, with a wide range of Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs, and Autism. Our school delivers a range of subjects, including the core subjects of English, maths and science, together with additional curriculum areas such as art, cooking, and creative and healthy curriculum.
We offer a structured environment centred on a meaningful and contextualised curriculum offer. Our clear purpose is to make an enduring difference to our learners’ lives, providing them with the knowledge, resilience and skills to enable them to have lasting employment and lifelong success. We aim to make them ‘life ready’.
At our school, we believe in the value and importance of building positive trusting relationships with young people to gain a deep understanding of each learner’s needs. This enables us to provide individually tailored provision which facilitates and supports each child’s unique way of learning. Learners are supported by highly qualified and skilled Teachers and Teaching Assistants, including through social skill time.
Young people are supported and enabled to make choices, informed by an understanding of the consequences of their decisions. Relationships are at the core of all we do at Kingfisher School. We believe that caring and respecting is what changes the behaviour of young people. We have a restorative, trauma informed approach.
Kingfisher School aims to work with learners who choose to be at the school. We aim to promote positive attitudes towards learning, so that young people enjoy school and feel safe and comfortable attending, thus acquiring a solid basis for lifelong learning.
We believe every experience is a learning experience and all staff maintain a non-judgemental approach to working with young people. We are always curious.
Our Offer
We are proud of the extensive services we provide to our learners and families, which include the following.
Our school’s ethos and aims are to uphold our Purpose, Mission, Vision and Values which are:
Our Purpose
To ensure every learner becomes life ready so that they can engage positively with society and independently advocate for themselves.
Our Mission
We will work in partnership with parents and professionals to allow every learner to be active in the community, becoming confident and prepared for their future beyond our school.
Our Vision
We provide high quality education delivered through a trauma informed therapeutic PACE (Playfulness, Acceptance, Curiosity and Empathy) approach.
Our Values
Education with equity at its heart.
Julie Jeanes - Principal, The Kingfisher School
With over 20 years of experience in education, I feel privileged to have the opportunity to lead our incredible school community as the Principal of Kingfisher.
My journey began after earning my degree in Dance, I found myself working in an outdoor pursuits centre in North Wales. It was there that I discovered a deep and lasting passion for supporting children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities, I went on to qualify as a teacher to be able to realise my vocation.
Since then, I’ve spent 15 years dedicated to working with SEND pupils, including 10 years as a SENDCo, and the last 5 years in senior leadership. Each step of the journey has strengthened my commitment to creating nurturing, inclusive environments where every young person is seen, heard, and empowered.
I believe wholeheartedly in the potential of every student. My vision is for our school to be a place where young people thrive, reach their academic potential and also grow in confidence, character, and self-belief. Our mission is to equip them with the skills, resilience, and aspirations they need to transition into the next stage of their lives, ready to make a positive impact in the world.
It is an honour to serve the young people and families in our community, and I am excited to continue this journey together.
Community and Charity
The school fosters an ethos of charitable work, taking part in fundraising and awareness events, including Comic Relief, Mental Health Awareness and Cancer Research UK.

Melrose Education strengthens wellbeing support for learners, families and colleagues
Melrose Education is continuing to strengthen its commitment to wellbeing across its family of specialist schools through the introduction of The Wellbeing Hub, an evidence-based online platform designed to support learners, families and colleagues.
The Wellbeing Hub, developed by Teen Tips, provides a wide range of expert-led resources, including webinars, podcasts, articles, practical guidance and wellbeing advice tailored for staff, parents and young people. The platform takes a proactive approach to mental health and emotional wellbeing, helping school communities build resilience, strengthen relationships and access trusted support whenever they need it.
Across Melrose Education, Wellbeing Champions are using the platform to signpost colleagues and families to high-quality resources, helping to promote positive wellbeing both in school and at home. By supporting the whole school community, the initiative reflects Melrose Education’s belief that the best outcomes for learners are achieved when families, colleagues and schools work together.
Tracey Storey, Founder, Executive Chair and CEO of Melrose Education, said:
“At Melrose Education, we know that wellbeing is fundamental to learning, development and success. By providing our Wellbeing Champions, colleagues and families with access to The Wellbeing Hub, we are investing in a proactive approach that supports our whole school communities. When learners, families and staff feel supported, connected and equipped with the right tools, everyone benefits.”
The introduction of The Wellbeing Hub forms part of Melrose Education’s wider commitment to creating positive, inclusive environments where learners can thrive academically, socially and emotionally, while ensuring families and colleagues have access to practical, evidence-based wellbeing support whenever they need it.

SEND
SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities) at Kingfisher School
Kingfisher School values the abilities and achievements of all its learners and is committed to providing every one of them with the best possible environment for learning, enabling them to thrive. We value the contribution that every learner makes and welcome a diversity of culture, religion and intellect. We are committed to offering an inclusive curriculum to ensure the best possible progress for all of our learners whatever their needs and abilities.
Kingfisher School seeks to raise the levels of attainment, remove barriers to learning, and increase curricular access to all. All learners are valued, respected and treated as equal members of the school. As such, provision for pupils with SEND is a matter for the school as a whole. Regular communication takes place between staff and our SENDCo, to identify young people who might need further assessment.
All learners have an Educational Support Plan (ESP) which outlines their specific challenges and how staff at Kingfisher School can support them to achieve these goals. Learners are involved in creating these plans and in reviewing and updating them on a termly basis, as they progress through the school. We work closely and collaboratively with parents and carers, ensuring consistent and ongoing discussions take place, as we understand the essential role this plays in every aspect of our special educational needs provision.
All our learners have an Education and Health Care Plan (EHCP). Our SENDCo leads on and completes the necessary paperwork for the annual review cycle for EHCPs and learners are involved in the Annual SEND Review meeting, so they can provide feedback on their education and progress. Our SENDCo shall also lead any on necessary emergency review processes.
Differentiated subject work, support programmes and assignments are implemented according to each learner’s needs and are delivered in the context of high quality teaching by our committed team of teachers and teaching assistants.
We work with a number of professionals including Speech and Language Therapists, CAMHS, Educational psychologists, and provide in-class support targeted at enabling learners to have access to the whole curriculum.

Curriculum
Our Curriculum Offer
At Kingfisher School, we pride ourselves on providing education that is engaging and innovative. We will always consider the specific needs of our learners and understand that they have not all had the best educational experience previously. We aim to inspire our learners to believe in their full potential, build confidence and resilience, and where appropriate, provide a pathway to reintegrate back into mainstream education. Our staff provide motivation, support, and guidance to our learners in every way possible to cater for their educational, social, and emotional needs, whilst raising their overall aspirations and personal self-esteem.
The school’s trauma informed, and restorative culture underpins all aspects of planning including curriculum intent, implementation and assessment, and supporting individuals to reach their full potential. Practices ensure that learners are fully supported with diverse opportunities to succeed where they may have previously experienced difficulty or failure.
Through a varied and adaptive curriculum, and the use of adaptive teaching methods, we aim to teach learners how to grow into positive, responsible young people who can have a positive impact on our local community, and successfully transition into further education, employment, volunteering, and adulthood. We value the spiritual and moral development of each person, as well as their intellectual and physical growth – the ability to participate positively in society is also at the heart of our planning. The development of social skills is promoted within our curriculum and throughout the school day, where elements such as self-esteem and self-awareness, body language, the way we talk, conversation and assertiveness are explored, modelled and practised.
Experiences in the community will give learners the opportunity to practise their skills in external situations with the support and care of our skilled staff team. We aim to make all our learners ‘life ready’.
Our curriculum promotes achievement and success regardless of starting point to build confidence and engagement. The curriculum is designed to ensure that all learners have the opportunity to fully achieve their potential and they will follow a variety of learning pathways that prepare them for suitable qualifications in KS4, including Entry Level, Functional skills, GCSE and BTEC. Our adaptive learning model supports progress and promotes independence through levels of classroom support.
Reading
Kingfisher School is committed to nurturing a culture of literacy proficiency and a love for reading. Through personalised strategies, a DfE-approved phonics scheme, and adaptive technology, we support each learner’s unique reading journey.
Staff have been fully trained and can deliver Twinkl Phonics for early readers alongside a phonics reading scheme aimed at secondary learners. Reading is promoted throughout the curriculum via engaging texts, learner choice, magazine subscriptions, library visits, and the use of Lexia for tailored reading instruction.
Lexia is an adaptive software which provides personalised reading instruction that targets gaps in phonics, vocabulary, and comprehension. Lexia supports independent learning and motivates pupils through interactive activities and regular progress milestones, enhancing both skill and enjoyment.
Support reading from early years through secondary
Vocational Pathways and Work Experience
Learners will have opportunities to undertake vocational activities where appropriate to needs and future aspirations. These courses are suitable for a wide range of learners of all abilities. The skills, knowledge and understanding gained during these courses also help learners prepare for work through real or simulated work situations. These qualifications aim to give learners a solid base to further develop their skills and learning.
Our aspirational careers and life skills programme will ensure our learners have experiences that set them up for independence and help them to realise their talents. This is under constant review to ensure it provides our learners with the very best chances for lifelong success.

Careers
Careers
At Kingfisher School, careers education, information, advice and guidance is a priority for ensuring learners move forward with the right tools and attitude to help prepare them for their future. Our varied and inclusive curriculum supports learners to consider their future options, realise their potential, be able to identify their skills, and transfer them to further education and the job market. Our dedicated Careers Lead at Kingfisher School is Cath Southerton.
We ensure that learners are motivated and excited for the world of work. We strive for high levels of expectations around self-confidence, emotional confidence and aspirations that are underpinned by our inclusive, tailored and robust PSHE curriculum.
We shall prepare learners, and liaise with parents and carers, for their preferred Post 16 pathway, whether that is to continue with further education, training or employment. We are fully committed to our statutory and moral obligation to provide a structured, varied and personalised careers education to all Key Stage 3 and Key Stage 4 learners.
Our Year 11 learners will have a range of opportunities for their Post 16 options, which includes continuing their education, moving on to local colleges or take apprenticeships.

We are committed to ensuring that wherever possible all learners are in education, employment or training post 16 and avoid becoming NEET (Not in Employment, Education, or Training).

Kingfisher School Enjoys Memorable Whole School Trip to Paultons Park
Learners and staff from Kingfisher School enjoyed an exciting whole school trip to Paultons Park, creating lasting memories and sharing a day filled with fun, laughter and adventure.
The visit provided learners with the opportunity to experience a wide range of rides and attractions while spending quality time with their peers and staff outside of the classroom environment. The school was fortunate to enjoy excellent weather throughout the day, and short queue times meant learners were able to make the most of everything the park had to offer.
Throughout the trip, learners demonstrated exemplary behaviour and were outstanding ambassadors for Kingfisher School. Their positive attitudes, kindness and enthusiasm were noted by staff, making the day a rewarding experience for everyone involved.
Educational visits such as these play an important role in supporting learners’ personal development, confidence and social skills, while also providing opportunities to build positive relationships and create shared experiences.
School Principal Julie Jeanes said:
“We are incredibly proud of all our learners for the way they represented Kingfisher School during our visit to Paultons Park. They demonstrated excellent behaviour, respect and enthusiasm throughout the day and were a credit to the school. It was wonderful to see everyone enjoying themselves, trying new experiences and making special memories together. A huge thank you to our staff team for helping to make the trip such a success.”
The trip was a fantastic success, and learners returned to school with plenty of stories to share following a brilliant day out.

PSHE and RSE
PSHE
At Kingfisher School our Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Curriculum is designed with the specific needs of our learners in mind and is reflective of Kingfisher aims and ethos. It is key in our support for leaners to attain emotional self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy and social skills.
PSHE makes a significant contribution to the promotion of young people’s personal and social development, enables them to know how to stay safe and healthy and teaches them how to manage their academic, personal and social lives in a positive way. Skills are developed that help our learners to grow and flourish as individuals and members of society.
Studying PSHE contributes to helping children and young people build their personal identities, confidence and self-esteem. It helps them to make career choices, understand and manage their finances, and what influences their decision making processes. PSHE enables learners to recognise their emotions and to communicate positively in a range of different scenarios.
Learners are taught and continually encouraged to respect other people, with particular regard to the protected characteristics set out in the Equality Act 2010. Learners study a variety of topics, which develop necessary skills and attributes, including, self-esteem, resilience, risk management and teamwork.
At Kingfisher School, we understand that PSHE lessons need to be fluid when dealing with topical situations in the lives of our learners, and current affairs that may affect them. We will not hesitate to change the content of lessons should the need arise, for example if a learner has lost a parent we will be sensitive when discussing families. If situations arise in the playground and a learner uses discriminatory language we will use our PSHE lessons to educate learners around this topic. We actively promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs, and our Careers Curriculum encourages learners to be citizens.
Our PSHE curriculum is planned around topics of:
· Self-Care, Support and Safety
· Changing and Growing
· Healthy lifestyles
· The World I Live In
RSE
At Kingfisher School, good relationships are fundamental to our ethos. Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) is lifelong learning about relationships, emotions, looking after ourselves, different families, sex, sexuality and sexual health. It involves acquiring information, developing skills and forming positive beliefs, values and attitudes. RSE has a key part to play in the personal, social, moral and spiritual development of young people.
There are five key elements that are covered in our curriculum:
· Respectful relationships including friendships
· Intimate and sexual relationships, including sexual health
Parents have the right to request children are removed from lessons teaching certain elements of RSE. Information on this can be downloaded here.

Year 8 Embarks on a Journey of Reflection at Bournemouth Tibetan Buddhist Centre
Year 8 learners recently enjoyed a thought-provoking and enriching visit to a Tibetan Buddhist Centre in Bournemouth as part of their Religious Education (RE) and Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) studies.
The visit provided a valuable opportunity for learners to deepen their understanding of different faiths, cultures and mindfulness practices through a range of immersive, hands-on experiences. The centre offered a unique sensory environment where learners could engage directly with Buddhist traditions and explore the importance of reflection, wellbeing and spiritual practice.
Throughout the visit, learners experienced a variety of sacred instruments and mindfulness activities. They took turns sounding the great gong and experimenting with singing bowls, discovering how different vibrations create calming and meditative sounds. Learners also used tingsha (finger bells), practising deep listening as they focused on the fading chimes and moments of silence.
A particular highlight of the visit was the opportunity to sit on traditional zafus (meditation cushions), where learners learned about meditation techniques and how posture can support relaxation, concentration and emotional wellbeing.
The experience brought classroom learning to life, helping learners develop a greater appreciation of diversity, respect for different beliefs and an understanding of mindfulness practices that can support positive mental health.
School Principal Julie Jeanes said:
“Visits such as this provide invaluable opportunities for our learners to engage with different cultures, beliefs and ways of thinking beyond the classroom. The learners approached the experience with curiosity, respect and maturity, and it was wonderful to see them fully immersed in the activities. The visit not only enhanced their understanding of Buddhism but also encouraged reflection, mindfulness and personal growth.”
The visit formed an important part of Kingfisher School’s wider curriculum, supporting learners to become informed, respectful and reflective members of their communities.

About Kingfisher School
Our School
Kingfisher School is a Special Educational Needs school which is located in Weymouth. We support learners aged 9 years to 16 years, with a wide range of Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs, and Autism. Our school delivers a range of subjects, including the core subjects of English, maths and science, together with additional curriculum areas such as art, cooking, and creative and healthy curriculum.
We offer a structured environment centred on a meaningful and contextualised curriculum offer. Our clear purpose is to make an enduring difference to our learners’ lives, providing them with the knowledge, resilience and skills to enable them to have lasting employment and lifelong success. We aim to make them ‘life ready’.
At our school, we believe in the value and importance of building positive trusting relationships with young people to gain a deep understanding of each learner’s needs. This enables us to provide individually tailored provision which facilitates and supports each child’s unique way of learning. Learners are supported by highly qualified and skilled Teachers and Teaching Assistants, including through social skill time.
Young people are supported and enabled to make choices, informed by an understanding of the consequences of their decisions. Relationships are at the core of all we do at Kingfisher School. We believe that caring and respecting is what changes the behaviour of young people. We have a restorative, trauma informed approach.
Kingfisher School aims to work with learners who choose to be at the school. We aim to promote positive attitudes towards learning, so that young people enjoy school and feel safe and comfortable attending, thus acquiring a solid basis for lifelong learning.
We believe every experience is a learning experience and all staff maintain a non-judgemental approach to working with young people. We are always curious.
Our Offer
We are proud of the extensive services we provide to our learners and families, which include the following.
Our school’s ethos and aims are to uphold our Purpose, Mission, Vision and Values which are:
Our Purpose
To ensure every learner becomes life ready so that they can engage positively with society and independently advocate for themselves.
Our Mission
We will work in partnership with parents and professionals to allow every learner to be active in the community, becoming confident and prepared for their future beyond our school.
Our Vision
We provide high quality education delivered through a trauma informed therapeutic PACE (Playfulness, Acceptance, Curiosity and Empathy) approach.
Our Values
Education with equity at its heart.
Julie Jeanes - Principal, The Kingfisher School
With over 20 years of experience in education, I feel privileged to have the opportunity to lead our incredible school community as the Principal of Kingfisher.
My journey began after earning my degree in Dance, I found myself working in an outdoor pursuits centre in North Wales. It was there that I discovered a deep and lasting passion for supporting children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities, I went on to qualify as a teacher to be able to realise my vocation.
Since then, I’ve spent 15 years dedicated to working with SEND pupils, including 10 years as a SENDCo, and the last 5 years in senior leadership. Each step of the journey has strengthened my commitment to creating nurturing, inclusive environments where every young person is seen, heard, and empowered.
I believe wholeheartedly in the potential of every student. My vision is for our school to be a place where young people thrive, reach their academic potential and also grow in confidence, character, and self-belief. Our mission is to equip them with the skills, resilience, and aspirations they need to transition into the next stage of their lives, ready to make a positive impact in the world.
It is an honour to serve the young people and families in our community, and I am excited to continue this journey together.
Community and Charity
The school fosters an ethos of charitable work, taking part in fundraising and awareness events, including Comic Relief, Mental Health Awareness and Cancer Research UK.
Our Latest News

Admissions
Applying for a Place at our School
To join our school, your child must have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) in place. Learners who are identified as having additional needs but do not yet have an EHCP, will need to undergo the Education, Health and Care Assessment Request (ECHAR) process. If capacity allows, Kingfisher School may support local authorities, families, and learners in gaining an EHCP by offering a short-term placement whilst all assessments are completed. If, following assessment, a learner is given an EHCP, admission will be considered to Kingfisher School in line with our Admissions Policy through coordination with the Local Authority.
We have a formal admissions procedure which is outlined in our Admissions Policy and which ensures we are able to meet a learner’s needs.
Our school supports learners with Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs and those who are on the Autistic Spectrum.
Learners can join our school at any time during the school year and will follow a personalised curriculum package to meet their individual needs.
Our caring and committed staff team will spend time getting to know you and your child during a carefully planned transition, to ensure they feel safe, settled, secure, and ready to learn.
Book a personalised tour by contacting the Principal. Or, alternatively, contact your current provision or Local Authority SEND Co-ordinator for more information about joining our unique and special school.
To read our Admissions Policy, please visit our Policies Page
Learner Case Studies
We love to celebrate our learners’ successes and achievements! We are proud to share with you some of the stories of how the school and our incredible team have supported learners to fulfil their potential.
Learner A joined Kingfisher in January 2025. A is Autistic and has a diagnosis of ADHD, with comorbid anxiety and depression, and an OT assessment completed at the end of the previous academic year identified significant sensory needs. When they arrived at Kingfisher, A was one of two learners in their Year 8 class and initially settled very well. As the group grew, however, the increased sensory and social demands became harder for them to manage, and their attendance began to decline. Staff responded with a range of strategies and, supported by the OT assessment, the school successfully secured additional 1:1 provision through an emergency EHCP review.
Despite ongoing challenges linked to overwhelm, A’s attendance this year shows meaningful progress from a starting point of complete disengagement from formal education. Their 86% attendance for 2024–2025 reflects a significant shift in their attitude towards school, especially compared with the 80.43% recorded in Autumn Term 1. A is a funny and intelligent young person who responds particularly well to 1:1 support, and they have built trusting relationships with key staff which have played a crucial role in their growing confidence. They are increasingly able to advocate for themselves and communicate their needs, something they struggled to do prior to joining Kingfisher.
This year, A has chosen to walk to school independently, a major step towards confidence and autonomy. Although this has affected their punctuality, staff recognise the wider positive impact of this development on their engagement. A’s mum describes a profound change since they joined Kingfisher, reflecting on how, before starting, A was unable to leave the house, no longer attended clubs, and had withdrawn from daily routines such as eating, washing, brushing their teeth, or getting dressed. Communication was minimal, and personal hygiene had almost stopped entirely. She explains that these areas began to transform once A started attending Kingfisher: they began getting up in the morning, getting dressed, brushing their teeth, and re-engaging with basic routines. She also shared that A is completely non-tactile due to past trauma and had not previously initiated physical affection, yet within their first term at Kingfisher they spontaneously hugged her three times—something she describes as hugely significant. A’s ability to recognise and articulate their emotions has consistently developed, despite previously being unable to identify even the simplest feelings.
A has also been able to build positive relationships with adults across the setting, including female staff, which had been particularly difficult for them in the past due to historical trauma. They now have two female teaching assistants with whom they feel safe and connected. Their journey demonstrates how a relationship-based, personalised and therapeutic approach can enable a young person with complex needs to rebuild trust in education, regain independence, and experience meaningful personal growth.
J has a diagnosis of ADHD and has experienced significant school-related trauma. Prior to joining Kingfisher, his attendance was variable, and he faced many challenges in engaging with school. Since joining, he has begun to make remarkable progress, building trust, confidence, and resilience with the support of a consistent, trusted adult and a trauma-informed approach.
J travels to school independently and demonstrates commitment by often being one of the first to arrive and the last to leave. Over the past year, he achieved more than 30 consecutive ‘green’ days, meeting all school expectations. This is a huge milestone reflecting both his determination and the strength of the home-school partnership.
He is gradually developing confidence in his abilities and showing compassion and empathy towards peers and staff. J is increasingly engaging in class discussions and written work, celebrating small successes, and responding positively to praise and structured, achievable tasks. Calm breaks and movement opportunities are supporting him to manage overwhelm and continue building his resilience.
J’s journey highlights the importance of a nurturing, consistent, and trauma-informed environment. With ongoing support, he is developing a more positive sense of identity as a learner, building confidence, and demonstrating that past challenges do not define his future potential.
H is an intelligent and funny young person with Autism and ADHD, alongside anxiety and depression. Before joining Kingfisher, he had not attended school for two years. Since starting with us, H has made remarkable progress, building confidence, independence, and strong relationships with trusted staff. He responds exceptionally well to 1:1 support and is now able to advocate for himself in ways he could not before.
H has also taken significant steps towards independence, including walking himself to school. This is a huge achievement and reflects his growing confidence and engagement with school life. With continued support, he is developing strategies to manage his emotions and sensory needs, ensuring he can thrive in his learning environment.
H’s mother has noticed the difference Kingfisher has made: “Since starting at Kingfisher, H began getting up, dressing, and even brushing his teeth. He has formed meaningful connections with staff, and his ability to recognise and articulate his emotions is consistently developing. The support he has received has genuinely changed both our lives.”
H’s journey highlights the impact of personalised support, nurturing relationships, and a school environment that enables learners to grow, develop independence, and engage with learning in a way that suits their individual needs.
Testimonials
I cannot express how grateful I am for this school. Every member of staff has been incredible: supportive, patient, and deeply understanding of the trauma she had faced. Through their care, communication, and consistent patience, she has not only settled but is truly excelling. The transformation has been remarkable—both at school and at home.
My child has been at Kingfisher for a year now, I cannot express how grateful I am for this school. The transformation has been remarkable—both at school and at home. She is now the happy, bright girl I fought so hard to protect, and I sincerely thank the Kingfisher team for helping her blossom.
My child started at Kingfisher School and came home after school for 2 weeks, he said I didn’t know schools like this existed. I feel like I walked through hell to get to heaven.
I don’t really know where to begin, but to say what a difference in Callum wanting to come to school because he feels so happy and comfortable in his new surroundings. I really wish there were more schools and staff like you all.
Kingfisher has afforded my child the chance to be seen, staff members endeavour to meet the needs of every child with inclusivity at the heart of everything they do!
Kingfisher is a fantastic school, accommodates every need of every learner. I for one can say moving my child here has benefited them in every way possible, helped them achieve their goals, makes friends and learn that school and learning can be fun.

Wellbeing and Mental Health
Wellbeing and Mental Health at Kingfisher School
At Kingfisher School we are committed to providing all our learners with rich and diverse experiences which promote their wellbeing, as well as their personal and social development.
We know that securing positive outcomes is dependent on promoting and prioritising positive mental health.
We ensure that all learners have a wellbeing check-in every morning before their day starts. This provides an opportunity for them to work through any concerns, worries or problems they may be experiencing – problems they may have encountered previously or during their journey into school. We want learners to feel confident, comfortable and ready for their learning to begin every day.
We offer additional support at lunch time for those learners who struggle with emotional regulation and need additional support to engage with their peers during social times.
We have a Wellbeing Lead in school who is here to support our staff team. Our Wellbeing Champion manages initiatives designed to promote a healthy and proactive environment to create a sense of community and belonging for all.
Young Minds
“We know parenting isn’t always easy. Although it’s often amazing and rewarding to watch your children grow up, and to help them learn to be independent, it can also be really hard work. It can feel especially hard if your child’s mood and behaviour seem different and you’re not sure why, or what you can do to help. But you are not alone.” (Young Minds 2020)”
Young Minds Parent Support
YoungMinds offers free confidential online and telephone support to anyone worried about the emotional and mental wellbeing of a child or young person up to the age of 25.
MindEd for Families
MindEd for Families is a branch of MindEd, intended to support parents and those caring for children and young people.
MindEd is an online e-portal offering free, simple advice about children and young people’s mental health for all adults.
Although MindEd is aimed at professionals, parents and carers may also find the information helpful.
Learners who are supported by Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS)
In an emergency contact your assigned crisis team – Monday to Friday 9am-5pm. Out of hours contact your GP.
Alternatively, for urgent mental health support contact Dorset Connection helpline on 0800 652 0190
Learners who are not supported by Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS)
If you need urgent help and you are not supported by CAMHS, call 111 and select the mental health option to speak to the 24-hour urgent mental health helpline.
Alternatively, contact Dorset Connection helpline on 0800 652 0190
Kooth Online Counselling
Kooth is a free, safe, confidential and non-stigmatised way for young people to receive counselling, advice, and support online 365 days a year.
Kooth is available for 11 – 25 year olds with the website available at all times at https://www.kooth.com/.
Counsellors are available to chat, Monday to Friday from 12:00pm to 10:00pm and on weekends, from 6:00pm to 10:00pm.
